questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field 'E' in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Energy stored = energy density × volume = $\dfrac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 E^2 \times (Ad)$.

questions.q: In the circuit shown in the figure, the potential difference across the 4μF capacitor is [Figure: a 4μF capacitor in series with a parallel combination of a 9μF and a 3μF capacitor, the series combination connected to a 12V battery]
questions.explanation: 9μF ∥ 3μF = 12μF; in series with 4μF, C$_{eq}$ = (4×12)/16 = 3μF. Charge Q = C$_{eq}$V = 3×12 = 36μC flows through the series branch, so V across 4μF = Q/4 = 9V.

questions.q: A 200 J of work is done in moving a charge 5C from a point A where the potential is - 20 V to another point B where potential is V volt. The value of V at B is
A potential at a point A is –3 V and that at another point B is 5 V. What is the work done in carrying a charge of 5 m C from B to A?

Match Column–I with Column–II related to an electric dipole of dipole moment $\vec p$ that is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec E$. Column–I (Angle between $\vec p$ and $\vec E$): a) 180° b) 120° c) 90°. Column–II (Potential energy of the dipole): i) –pE ii) pE iii) $\tfrac12$pE iv) Zero
options: a – ii, b – iii, c – iv
a – i, b – ii, c – iii
a – ii, b – iii, c – i
a – ii, b – i, c – iv
questions.explanation: $U=-pE\cos\theta$. At $180^\circ$, $U=pE$ (ii); at $120^\circ$, $U=-pE(-\tfrac12)=\tfrac12pE$ (iii); at $90^\circ$, $U=0$ (iv).

questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Electric field is always perpendicular to an equipotential surface.
Work done to move a charge on an equipotential surface is not zero
Equipotential surfaces are the surfaces where the potential is constant
Equipotential surfaces for a uniform electric field are parallel and equidistant from each other.
questions.explanation: Since the potential does not change along an equipotential surface, the work done moving a charge on it is always zero — so statement (2) is the false one.

questions.q: A cube of side 1 cm contains 100 molecules each having an induced dipole moment of $0.2\times10^{-6}\,C-m$ in an external electric field of $4\,NC^{-1}$. The electric susceptibility of the materials is _____ $C^2N^{-1}m^{-2}$

A capacitor of capacitance $5\mu F$ is charged by a battery of emf 10V. At an instant of time, the potential difference across the capacitors is 4V and the time rate of change of potential difference across the capacitor is $0.6\,Vs^{-1}$. Then the time rate at which energy is stored the capacitor at the instant is
questions.explanation: $u=\dfrac12CV^2\Rightarrow\dfrac{du}{dt}=CV\dfrac{dV}{dt}=5\times10^{-6}\times4\times0.6=12\mu W$.

questions.q: A uniform electric field vector $\vec E$ exists along horizontal direction as shown [field lines point rightward; a small charge q is slowly taken from point A along a curved (wavy) path to point B, where B is displaced horizontally by distance x from A]. The electric potential at A is V$_A$. A small point charge q is slowly taken from A to B along the curved path as shown. The potential energy of the charge when it is at point B is
questions.explanation: Since the field points from A towards B, the potential drops by Ex over that horizontal displacement, so V$_B$=V$_A$−Ex, giving potential energy U = q[V$_A$−Ex].

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance C$_1$ with a dielectric slab in between its plates is connected to a battery. It has a potential difference V$_1$ across its plates. When the dielectric slab is removed, keeping the capacitor connected to the battery, the new capacitance and potential difference are C$_2$ and V$_2$ respectively. Then,
questions.explanation: Since the capacitor stays connected to the battery, the potential difference is fixed by the battery (V$_1$=V$_2$); removing the dielectric decreases capacitance, so C$_1$>C$_2$.

questions.q: Five capacitors each of value 1 μF are connected as shown in the figure [two 1μF capacitors in series from A form the top and bottom arms of a bridge, one 1μF capacitor bridges the midpoints, and two more 1μF capacitors in series form the arms leading to B, symmetric about the bridging capacitor]. The equivalent capacitance between A and B is
questions.explanation: By symmetry of the balanced bridge network, no charge flows through the bridging capacitor, and the two series-parallel branches (each two 1 μF capacitors in series, giving 0.5 μF, in parallel with each other) combine to give an equivalent capacitance of 1 μF between A and B.

questions.q: The electric field and the potential of an electric dipole vary with distance r as
questions.explanation: For an electric dipole, the field falls off as $1/r^3$ and the potential falls off as $1/r^2$.

questions.q: Two tiny spheres carrying charges 1.8 $\mu$C and 2.8 $\mu$C are located at 40 cm apart. The potential at the mid-point of the line joining the two charges is
questions.explanation: At the mid-point, $r=0.2$ m from each charge. $V=k\dfrac{q_1+q_2}{r}=9\times10^9\times\dfrac{4.6\times10^{-6}}{0.2}\approx2.1\times10^5$ V.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting a 2 V battery across it. It is then disconnected from the battery and a glass slab is introduced between plates. Which of the following pairs of quantities decrease?
questions.explanation: With the battery disconnected, charge Q stays constant while inserting the dielectric increases capacitance C; since $V=Q/C$ and $U=Q^2/2C$, both the potential difference and the stored energy decrease.

questions.q: If a slab of insulating material (conceptual) 4 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ m thick is introduced between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor, the separation between the plates has to be increased by 3.5 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ m to restore the capacity to original value. The dielectric constant of the material will be
questions.explanation: $\Delta d = t\left(1-\dfrac1K\right) \Rightarrow 3.5\times10^{-3}=4\times10^{-3}\left(1-\dfrac1K\right)\Rightarrow K=8$.

questions.q: Eight drops of mercury of equal radii combine to form a big drop. The capacitance of a bigger drop as compared to each smaller drop is
questions.explanation: Volume conservation gives $R=2r$ (since $8\times\tfrac43\pi r^3=\tfrac43\pi R^3$). Since $C\propto r$, the capacitance becomes 2 times.

questions.q: Which of the statements is false in the case of polar molecules?
options: Centers of positive and negative charges are separated in the absence of external electric field.
Centers of positive and negative charges are separated in the presence of external electric field.
Do not possess permanent dipole moments.
Ionic molecule HCl is the example of polar molecule.
questions.explanation: Polar molecules do possess permanent dipole moments even without an external field, so statement (C) is false.

questions.q: An electrician requires a capacitance of 6 μF in a circuit across a potential difference of 1.5 kV. A large number of 2 μF capacitors which can withstand a potential difference of not more than 500 V are available. The minimum number of capacitors required for the purpose is
questions.explanation: 3 capacitors in series (500 V each) withstand 1500 V and give $\tfrac{2}{3}\ \mu$F; to get 6 μF total, 9 such series strings are needed in parallel: $9\times3=27$ capacitors.

questions.q: In figure, charge on the capacitor is plotted against potential difference across the capacitor: a straight line through the origin reaching Q = 120 μC at V = 10 V. The capacitance and energy stored in the capacitor are respectively.
questions.explanation: $C=\dfrac{Q}{V}=\dfrac{120}{10}=12\ \mu$F; Energy $=\tfrac12CV^2=\tfrac12(12\times10^{-6})(10)^2=600\ \mu$J.

questions.q: When a soap bubble is charged?
options: Its radius may increase or decrease.
questions.explanation: Charging a soap bubble adds an outward electrostatic pressure $\sigma^2/2\varepsilon_0$ on the surface, so to maintain equilibrium the bubble expands, i.e. its radius increases.

questions.q: [Figure shows a capacitor network between A and B: a 50 pF capacitor forms the top branch; a series combination of two 100 pF capacitors forms the middle branch ending at A; a 50 pF capacitor forms the bottom branch ending at B, with the top and middle branches joined together] The equivalent capacitance between A and B is,
questions.explanation: The two 100 pF capacitors in series give 50 pF, which combines in parallel with the top 50 pF branch to give 100 pF; this 100 pF is then in series with the bottom 50 pF, giving $\dfrac{100\times50}{150} = \dfrac{100}{3}$ pF.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance C charged by an amount Q is connected in parallel with an uncharged capacitor of capacitance 2C. The final charges on the capacitors are
questions.explanation: Total charge Q is conserved and redistributes in proportion to capacitance across the two capacitors in parallel: $Q_1 = Q\times\dfrac{C}{3C} = Q/3$ and $Q_2 = Q\times\dfrac{2C}{3C} = 2Q/3$.

questions.q: [Graph shows electric potential V in volts (y-axis) versus distance x in metres (x-axis): V = 2 V (constant) for region A from x=0 to 1; V rises linearly from 2 to 4 for region B from x=1 to 2; V = 4 V (constant) for region C from x=2 to 4; V falls linearly from 4 to 0 for region D from x=4 to 5] The figure gives the electric potential V as a function of distance through four regions on x-axis. Which of the following is true for the magnitude of the electric field E in these regions ?
questions.explanation: $E=-dV/dx$: in the flat regions A and C, E = 0 (so E$_A$ = E$_C$); in region B the slope magnitude is 2, and in region D it is 4, so E$_B$ < E$_D$.

questions.q: A system of two charges separated by a certain distance apart stores electrical potential energy. If the distance between them is increased, the potential energy of the system,
questions.explanation: PE $= kq_1q_2/r$; if the charges are of the same sign, PE is positive and decreases as r increases, but if of opposite sign, PE is negative and increases (towards zero) as r increases, so the PE may increase or decrease.

questions.q: A mass of 1 kg carrying a charge of 2 C is accelerated through a potential of 1 V. The velocity acquired by it is
For the arrangement of capacitors as shown in the circuit, the effective capacitance between the points A and B is (capacitance of each capacitor is 4 $\mu$F)
questions.note: By direct circuit analysis: A is wired directly to both the top-left and bottom-left corners, so the top 4$\mu$F (A to B) and bottom 4$\mu$F (A to B) are in parallel, giving 8 $\mu$F between A and B; the remaining two 4$\mu$F capacitors plus the rightmost 4$\mu$F form a triangle hanging off B with no other external connection, so by symmetry they carry no charge and don't affect the result. This computation gives 8 $\mu$F (option D), not 4 $\mu$F, but KEA's official answer is option A.
questions.explanation: The KEA key gives option A, 4 $\mu$F.

questions.q: The work done to move a charge on an equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: Since all points on an equipotential surface are at the same potential, the potential difference is zero, so the work done in moving a charge on it is zero.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 3 $\mu$F and 6 $\mu$F are connected in series and a potential difference of 900 V is applied across the combination. They are then disconnected and reconnected in parallel. The potential difference across the combination is
questions.explanation: In series, charge Q = C$_{series}$V = 2 × 900 = 1800 $\mu$C on each capacitor. Reconnecting in parallel: if the like-charged plates are joined, V = (Q+Q)/(C$_1$+C$_2$) = 3600/9 = 400 V, but if the oppositely-charged plates are joined the charges cancel giving 0 V; the KEA key accepted both 0 V and 400 V (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Two point charges A = +3 nC and B = +1 nC are placed 5 cm apart in air. The work done to move charge B towards A by 1 cm is
questions.explanation: $W = kq_1q_2\left(\dfrac{1}{r_f}-\dfrac{1}{r_i}\right) = 9\times10^9\times3\times10^{-9}\times1\times10^{-9}\left(\dfrac{1}{0.04}-\dfrac{1}{0.05}\right) = 1.35\times10^{-7}$ J.

questions.q: A system of 2 capacitors of capacitance 2 μF and 4 μF is connected in series across a potential difference of 6V. The electric charge and energy stored in the system are
questions.explanation: $C_{eq} = \dfrac{2\times4}{2+4} = \dfrac{4}{3}\,\mu$F. Charge $Q = C_{eq}V = \dfrac{4}{3}\times6 = 8\,\mu$C. Energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}C_{eq}V^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{4}{3}\times36 = 24\,\mu$J.

questions.q: The minimum value of effective capacitance that can be obtained by combining 3 capacitors of capacitances 1 pF, 2 pF and 4 pF is
questions.explanation: Minimum capacitance is obtained connecting all in series: $\dfrac{1}{C} = 1+\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{7}{4} \Rightarrow C=\dfrac{4}{7}$ pF.

questions.q: Nature of equipotential surface for a point charge is
options: Sphere with charge at the centre of the sphere.
Sphere with charge on the surface of the sphere.
Plane with charge on the surface.
questions.explanation: For a point charge, potential $V=kq/r$ is constant on any sphere centred at the charge, so equipotential surfaces are concentric spheres with the charge at the centre.

questions.q: A particle of mass 1 gm and charge 1 $\mu$C is held at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface at distance 1 m from the fixed charge 2 mC. If the particle is released, it will be repelled. The speed of the particle when it is at a distance of 10 m from the fixed charge
questions.explanation: By energy conservation, $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2=kQq\left(\dfrac1{r_1}-\dfrac1{r_2}\right)=9\times10^9\times2\times10^{-3}\times10^{-6}(1-0.1)=16.2$ J, giving $v=\sqrt{2\times16.2/10^{-3}}=180$ ms$^{-1}$.

questions.q: A capacitor of 8 F is connected as shown. Charge on the plates of the capacitor [Figure: three parallel branches between the same two nodes — top branch: 8 F capacitor in series with 20 Ω; middle branch: 4 Ω resistor; bottom branch: 5 V cell in series with 1 Ω]
questions.explanation: In steady state no current flows in the capacitor branch, so no drop across its 20 Ω; the capacitor sees the same voltage as across the 4 Ω branch. Current in the 5 V loop: $I=5/(1+4)=1$ A, so voltage across the 4 Ω (= across capacitor) is 4 V. Charge $=CV=8\times4=32$ C.

questions.q: Four metal plates are arranged as shown. Capacitance between X and Y (A -> Area of each plate, d -> distance between the plates) [Figure: four identical parallel plates 1, 2, 3, 4 stacked with equal spacing d; plate 1 connects to X, plate 3 connects to Y, and plates 2 and 4 are joined together by a connecting wire]
questions.explanation: With plates 2 and 4 tied together as a common node M, the gap 1-2 gives a capacitor $C_0=\epsilon_0A/d$ between X and M, while the gaps 2-3 and 3-4 give two capacitors $C_0$ in parallel between M and Y (total $2C_0$); these combine in series (X-M-Y) to give $C_{eq}=\dfrac{C_0\cdot2C_0}{C_0+2C_0}=\dfrac{2}{3}C_0$.

questions.q: Three point charges 3 nC, 6 nC and 9 nC are placed at the corners of an equilateral triangle of side 0.1 m. The potential energy of the system is
questions.explanation: $U=\dfrac{k(q_1q_2+q_2q_3+q_1q_3)}{r}=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times(18+54+27)\times10^{-18}}{0.1}=8.91\times10^{-6}$ J. The numeric value 8910 (properly in nJ, not J as printed) matches option (1); the unit error in the printed options is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark here (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A spherical shell of radius 10 cm is carrying a charge q. If the electric potential at distances 5 cm, 10 cm and 15 cm from the centre of the spherical shell is $V_1$, $V_2$ and $V_3$ respectively, then
questions.explanation: Inside a charged shell the potential is constant and equal to the surface potential ($V_1=V_2$), while outside it falls as 1/r, so $V_3 < V_1 = V_2$.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged and then isolated. The effect of increasing the plate separation on charge, potential and capacitance respectively are
questions.explanation: An isolated capacitor keeps charge Q constant; increasing separation decreases capacitance $C=\varepsilon_0A/d$, so $V=Q/C$ increases.

questions.q: What is the electric potential at a distance of 9 cm from 3 nC?

A voltmeter reads 4 V when connected to a parallel plate capacitor with air as a dielectric. When a dielectric slab is introduced between plates for the same configuration, voltmeter reads 2 V. What is the dielectric constant of the material?
questions.explanation: For constant charge, K = V$_0$/V = 4/2 = 2.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 10 PF and 20 PF are connected to 200 V and 100 V sources respectively. If they are connected by the wire, what is the common potential of the capacitors?

Two metal spheres of radii 0.01 m and 0.02 m are given a charge of 15 mC and 45 mC respectively. They are then connected by a wire. The final charge on the first sphere is ______ $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ C.
questions.explanation: Connecting the spheres by a wire brings them to the same potential, so the total charge (60 mC) divides in the ratio of their radii: $Q_1=\dfrac{0.01}{0.01+0.02}\times60=20\times10^{-3}$ C.

questions.q: Two concentric spheres of radii R and r have positive charges q$_1$ and q$_2$ with equal surface charge densities. What is the electric potential at their common centre ?
questions.explanation: Both shells contribute to the centre's potential: $V=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\dfrac{q_1}{R}+\dfrac{q_2}{r}\right)$. Using $q=\sigma\times4\pi(\text{radius})^2$ for each shell gives $V=\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}(R+r)$.

questions.q: When an additional charge of 2C is given to a capacitor, energy stored in it is increased by 21%. The original charge of the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Energy $U=q^2/2C$. $(q+2)^2=1.21q^2\Rightarrow q+2=1.1q\Rightarrow q=20$ C.

questions.q: When a potential difference of 10$^3$ V is applied between A and B, a charge of 0.75 mC is stored in the system of capacitors as shown. The value of C is (in $\mu$F) [a quadrilateral capacitor bridge: the top side has two 2 $\mu$F capacitors in series through a midpoint node; the bottom side has one 2 $\mu$F capacitor; the right side has one 2 $\mu$F capacitor; a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner carries the unknown capacitor C; the 10$^3$ V source connects the bottom-left corner (A) to the top-left corner (B)]
questions.explanation: Writing charge-conservation (node) equations for this capacitor bridge with the given source and requiring the total charge drawn to equal 0.75 mC gives C = 2 $\mu$F.

questions.q: See the diagram. Area of each plate is 2.0 m$^2$ and d = 2 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ m. A charge of 8.85 $\times$ 10$^{-8}$ C is given to Q. Then the potential of Q becomes [three parallel plates P, Q, R; the gap between P and Q is d, and the gap between Q and R is 2d; P and R are both connected to ground]
questions.explanation: The charge on the isolated middle plate Q splits between its two faces inversely with distance (since both P and R are grounded): the face towards P (gap $d$) carries $\dfrac23$ of the total charge. $V_Q=\dfrac{q_{top}\,d}{\epsilon_0 A}=\dfrac{(2/3)(8.85\times10^{-8})(2\times10^{-3})}{8.85\times10^{-12}\times2}\approx6.67$ V.

questions.q: In this diagram, the P.D. between A and B is 60 V [figure: A -- 6$\mu$F -- 3$\mu$F -- (two 3$\mu$F capacitors in parallel) -- 3$\mu$F -- B, all in series]. The P.D. across 6 $\mu$F capacitor is .....V
questions.explanation: The four series sections (6, 3, [3||3]=6, 3 $\mu$F) combine to a series equivalent of 1 $\mu$F, so charge Q = 1$\mu$F$\times$60 V = 60 $\mu$C; P.D. across the 6 $\mu$F capacitor = Q/C = 60/6 = 10 V.

questions.q: Two fixed charges A and B of 5 $\mu$C each are separated by a distance of 6 m. C is the mid point of the line joining A and B. A charge 'Q' of -5 $\mu$C is shot perpendicular to the line joining A and B through C with a kinetic energy of 0.06 J. The charge 'Q' comes to rest at a point D. The distance CD is
questions.explanation: By energy conservation, KE + U(C) = U(D) where $U(x)=\dfrac{2kq_Aq_Q}{\sqrt{9+x^2}}$; solving $0.06-0.15=-0.45/\sqrt{9+x^2}$ gives $\sqrt{9+x^2}=5$, so x = 4 m.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 10 $\mu$F is charged to 10 V. The energy stored in it is
questions.explanation: $U=\dfrac12CV^2=\dfrac12\times10\times10^{-6}\times10^2=500\ \mu$J.

questions.q: In the given network, the value of $C$, so that an equivalent capacitance between $A$ and $B$ is $3\mu F$, is ................. [Network of capacitors between A and B arranged in a ladder of series-parallel combinations involving capacitors $C$, $2\mu F$, $6\mu F$, $12\mu F$, $4\mu F$, $2\mu F$, $1\mu F$, $2\mu F$ and $8\mu F$]
questions.explanation: Reducing the ladder network of fixed capacitors stage by stage (series and parallel combinations) and equating the resulting series combination with $C$ to the required 3 uF between A and B gives $C=48\,\mu F$ (as per KEA key).

questions.q: There is a uniform electric field of intensity $E$ which is as shown [four horizontal rows of points with field lines pointing right; the fully shaded point is the 2nd point in the 2nd row]. How many labelled points have the same electric potential as the fully shaded point?
questions.explanation: Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to $E$, i.e. vertical lines here; so all points in the same column as the shaded point are at the same potential — that column has 3 other points.

questions.q: All capacitors used in the diagram are identical and each is of capacitance $C$ [three parallel branches connect $A$ to $B$; each branch contains two capacitors in series]. Then the effective capacitance between the points $A$ and $B$ is .....................
questions.explanation: Each branch (two capacitors in series) has capacitance $C/2$; three such branches in parallel give $3\times C/2=1.5C$.

questions.q: [Circuit: a 12 V battery in series with a $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor, which is in series with a parallel combination of $4\ \mu\text{F}$ and $2\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitors, forming a closed loop.] The charge deposited on $4\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Parallel combination $=4+2=6\ \mu\text{F}$, in series with $6\ \mu\text{F}$ gives $C_{eq}=3\ \mu\text{F}$; total charge $=3\times12=36\ \mu\text{C}$, so voltage across the parallel pair $=36/6=6$ V, giving charge on $4\ \mu\text{F}$ $=4\times6=24\ \mu\text{C}$.

questions.q: The electric potential at any point x, y, z in metres is given by $V = 3x^2$. The electric field at a point (2 m, 0, 1 m) is
